Mika —

Appreciate the sample traffic. Short answer: most prefix-cache hits are not charged per-token when they are served purely from a warm cache that returns an identical token sequence without triggering model compute. But there are important exceptions and bookkeeping rules — I laid these out with explicit examples below.

Example 1 — Exact prefix + identical generation (cache hit, no billed tokens):
Request: [PREFIX = 120 tokens static instructions] + [USER = "Summarize the following conversation" 30 tokens]
If prefix+prompt+model config matches an existing cached response and we return the cached token sequence, you are not billed for per-token generation for those returned tokens (we only account for a small read charge). Result: billed only for storage/metadata at negligible cost.

Example 2 — Prefix match but temperature/stop tokens differ (computes, billed):
If the client changes generation parameters (temperature, top_k, stop sequences) we may not be able to reuse the cached output; runtime will do generation and standard per-token billing applies.

Example 3 — Partial prefix reuse (KV cache reuse during autoregressive generation — billed for new tokens):
If the prefix matches cached KV keys, we can avoid recomputing early layers, but the system still streams new tokens and those newly-generated tokens are billed. In practice: you pay for the delta tokens produced after the cached prefix; the cached prefix itself is not billed again.

Edge case — Session affinity & short lived caches:
- Warm prefetch: when we warm a cache in anticipation of requests (not served result directly) there is no per-request billing; warming is part of runtime ops and covered in ratecard allowance for prefetch on committed plans.
- Evicted cache entries: if an entry is evicted and later re-generated, that generation is billed like any other request.

I'll attach a short spreadsheet/ratecard excerpt (see attached redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf) and a recommended commit tier for your traffic. For your $1.2M ARR target and the prefix-heavy shape, we propose a committed plan that bundles a prefetched cache allowance and a lower per-token rate for deltas.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben — can you include a proforma commit tier and estimated monthly burn for Brightpoint using their sample traffic?
2) If Brightpoint is willing to commit, we can add a specific cache-prefetch allowance and a contract clause that clarifies billing for cache hits vs delta tokens.

Thanks,

- Billing model we should propose: base compute committed tokens + delta-token metering for generations that reuse KV cache. Add a prefetch allowance (X tokens/month) tied to the commit.

Suggested numbers for a $1.2M ARR committment (annualized):

- Prefetch allowance: 150M prefetched-token-equivalents / month (not billed per-hit while resident)
- Delta-token rate: $0.000008 per token (vs list $0.000012)
- Contract clause: cache-hit definition requires identical model config + no live stop/temperature differences; prefetch warming covered by Redwood ops up to allowance.

Ben/Team —
I drafted a short amendment for the SOW that:
- Defines "cache-hit" as: identical prefix hash + identical model config + identical temperature/top_k/stop sequences; when true, returning a cached response is not billed for per-token generation.
- Defines "delta tokens": tokens produced after levered KV-cache reuse; billed at the delta rate.
- Includes prefetched-token allowance and outlines eviction behavior + notifications if prefetch allowance exceeded.

I'll attach the amendment text below (also put in the docx Ben attached). If that looks good we can attach it to the draft SOW and send to Mika.

---
Amendment excerpt: "Prefetch Allowance & Cache Billing — Redwood will provide a monthly prefetched-token allowance to Customer as specified in the Schedule. For cache hits that meet the Cache-hit definition, Redwood will not charge per-token generation fees for the cached output returned directly from the resident cache. Customer will be billed for Delta Tokens generated after KV-cache reuse at the Delta Token Rate. Redwood will notify Customer when cache eviction events may materially affect hit rates."
